title: Windows System Audit Policy Changes (Event 4719)
exclusions: This rule reports Microsoft Security Event ID 4719 for every observed local system audit-policy subcategory change. It does not cover object SACL changes (4715/4817/4907), per-user policy (4912), event-source registration (4904/4905), CrashOnAuditFail (4906), audit-policy security-descriptor changes, Security-log clearing (1102), service/configuration tampering, or process command lines such as `auditpol.exe /set`. It does not prove that Group Policy was the origin, that the subject account identifies the human requester, that logging was weakened, or that an adversary acted. Missing endpoint telemetry and pre-coverage changes remain invisible. No regulation or runtime assurance is claimed.
evidence: After deployment, retain the version-controlled `windows_system_audit_policy_change_4719` saved-search definition and ACL; schedule, dispatch, and triggered-alert history; every result row with endpoint, subject SID/name/domain/logon ID, category and subcategory IDs/GUID, raw and decoded change, event record ID, source, and source type; corresponding raw 4719 XML; effective Advanced Audit Policy/GPO and `auditpol /get` output; Splunk input and add-on version; endpoint/source-health results; dated positive and negative controls; alert delivery; analyst disposition; and any bounded notification exception. This documentation-only review generated no policy change, Windows event, Splunk job, alert, or production evidence.

controlTest.positiveScenario: In an isolated test index and fixed time range, replay one XML Security record with `source=XmlWinEventLog:Security`, `sourcetype=XmlWinEventLog`, `EventCode=4719`, `Computer=WIN-4719.example`, `EventRecordID=9001`, `SubjectUserSid=S-1-5-18`, `SubjectUserName=WIN-4719$`, `SubjectDomainName=EXAMPLE`, `SubjectLogonId=0x3e7`, `CategoryId=%%8274`, `SubcategoryId=%%12807`, `SubcategoryGuid={0CCE9223-69AE-11D9-BED3-505054503030}`, and `AuditPolicyChanges=%%8448, %%8450`. Expect exactly one row with endpoint `win-4719.example` and change summary `Success removed; Failure removed`. Documentation review checks the expected transformation but does not claim replay.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Run isolated variants and expect zero rows for each: Security Event ID 4715, 4906, 4912, or 1102; Event ID 4719 under `source=XmlWinEventLog:System`; a 4719 Classic-rendered event under a different source type; a malformed record whose `EventCode` and `EventID` are not numeric 4719; an admitted event with empty `Computer`, `dest`, and `host`; an event at or after the exclusive latest boundary; and a 4719 outside the selected closed hour. A valid 4719 with `%%8449` (Success added) must produce one row, proving this rule monitors all system audit-policy changes rather than only disabling changes.

dataSources: Microsoft-Windows-Security-Auditing Event ID 4719 from each supported Windows endpoint's Security channel, collected in XML by Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows (`Splunk_TA_windows`, Splunkbase 742) version 10.0.1. The deployment-local example uses `index=wineventlog`; the supported XML contract is `sourcetype=XmlWinEventLog`, `source=XmlWinEventLog:Security`. Required native fields are `EventCode` or `EventID`, `Computer`, `EventRecordID`, `SubjectUserSid`, `SubjectUserName`, `SubjectDomainName`, `SubjectLogonId`, `CategoryId`, `SubcategoryId`, `SubcategoryGuid`, and `AuditPolicyChanges`; the rendered fallback can expose `Changes`. Microsoft documents `%%8448` Success removed, `%%8449` Success added, `%%8450` Failure removed, and `%%8451` Failure added.
app: Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows (`Splunk_TA_windows`, Splunkbase 742), version 10.0.1, for XML Security-channel collection and field knowledge. Splunkbase lists that release for Splunk Enterprise 9.3 through current 10.x releases and Splunk Cloud with CIM 5.x at review time. Test upgrades, especially from releases before the documented 5.0.0 breaking-change boundary. No premium app is required; Splunk Enterprise Security can optionally create findings.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="XmlWinEventLog" source="XmlWinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4719 earliest=-70m@m latest=-10m@m
| eval event_code=tonumber(coalesce(EventCode,EventID)), endpoint=lower(trim(coalesce(dest,Computer,host))), subject_account=if(len(trim(SubjectDomainName))>0,trim(SubjectDomainName)."\\".trim(SubjectUserName),trim(SubjectUserName)), raw_policy_change=coalesce(AuditPolicyChanges,Changes)
| where event_code=4719 AND len(endpoint)>0
| eval change_summary=case(raw_policy_change="%%8448","Success removed",raw_policy_change="%%8449","Success added",raw_policy_change="%%8450","Failure removed",raw_policy_change="%%8451","Failure added",raw_policy_change="%%8448, %%8450","Success removed; Failure removed",raw_policy_change="%%8449, %%8451","Success added; Failure added",true(),raw_policy_change), detection="Windows system audit policy changed"
| table _time endpoint subject_account SubjectUserSid SubjectLogonId CategoryId SubcategoryId SubcategoryGuid raw_policy_change change_summary EventRecordID detection source sourcetype
| sort 0 -_time endpoint SubcategoryGuid
description: Reports one row for each Windows Security Event ID 4719 in the delayed closed hour, at endpoint and changed-subcategory-event grain. The row preserves the subject token, category/subcategory identifiers, GUID, raw policy-change codes, decoded addition/removal meaning, and event identity.
value: Audit policy determines which security-relevant actions leave evidence. Prompt review of every change helps defenders distinguish authorized policy rollout from accidental coverage loss or deliberate defense impairment, restore required telemetry, and preserve confidence in incident and audit records. This improves assurance that later investigations have the audit evidence the approved policy was meant to retain.
implementation: Collect every endpoint's Security channel in XML with Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows 10.0.1 and validate native 4719 fields before alerting. Save the SPL as `windows_system_audit_policy_change_4719`, run hourly over the delayed closed window `-70m@m` to `-10m@m`, and trigger on any row. Route removals and high-value assets urgently; route approved additions or GPO convergence to review without discarding the base event. Resolve each SubcategoryGuid against a version-controlled export from `auditpol /list /subcategory:* /v`.
visualization: On a restricted audit-integrity dashboard, put endpoint Security-source health and policy-inventory coverage first. Add a single value for changed endpoints; stacked counts of added versus removed Success/Failure settings; a timeline by endpoint and subcategory GUID; and a table with subject account/SID/logon ID, category/subcategory, decoded change, EventRecordID, owner, and change ticket. Drilldown should open raw 4719 XML, same-logon events, effective `auditpol /get` evidence, GPO operational records, and recent process telemetry without attributing a human solely from the subject field.
schema: Microsoft-Windows-Security-Auditing Event ID 4719 native XML fields, with optional Splunk Common Information Model Change normalization
dataModelAcceleration: Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows documents Event ID 4719 mappings including Change-oriented fields such as `change_type`, `object`, `object_attrs`, `result`, `user`, and `dest`. No accelerated replacement is supplied because the native `SubjectUserSid`, `SubjectLogonId`, `CategoryId`, `SubcategoryId`, `SubcategoryGuid`, exact `AuditPolicyChanges`, and `EventRecordID` are required to interpret and evidence this rule. A generic `Change.All_Changes` search can mix unrelated object changes. If a local CIM search is added, filter normalized signature/event ID 4719 and prove row/field parity against raw XML.

knownFalsePositives:
A result is a genuine 4719 policy-change record. “False positive” means the change is authorized or expected, not that the Security event is false.

1. **Active Directory Group Policy `gpupdate` convergence** — Applying Advanced Audit Policy Configuration can emit multiple 4719 records, often under LocalSystem/computer-account context. Confirm the winning GPO, GroupPolicy Operational log, Resultant Set of Policy, domain-controller replication, approved change ID, expected GUID/value set, and UTC rollout window. Suppress notification only for the exact GPO/version/target window; keep the events.

2. **Microsoft Intune security baseline or Configuration Manager compliance policy** — Endpoint-management rollout can add or restore audit subcategories. Match policy/profile ID, assignment group, deployment status, endpoint set, operator, expected before/after export, and change approval. Do not allowlist Intune-enrolled hosts globally because a compromised policy can change the same settings.

3. **Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, CIS benchmark, or DISA STIG hardening deployment** — Onboarding or remediation scripts may set required Success/Failure auditing. Verify signed package, baseline revision, script hash, affected SubcategoryGuids, maintenance window, and post-change compliance. Use a finite rollout exception and investigate any removal not present in the approved manifest.

4. **Local `auditpol.exe` repair by Windows platform engineering** — An administrator may restore drift or test a policy. Correlate same-logon 4688/process telemetry, ticket, operator, command line, endpoint, exact GUID, and a post-change `auditpol /get` export. Never suppress merely because SubjectUserName is an administrator or computer account.

5. **Domain join, promotion, re-image, or role-baseline transition** — Provisioning systems can replace a local baseline when a machine joins a domain or becomes a domain controller. Confirm build workflow, asset lifecycle state, GPO application, expected final policy, and source-health continuity. Limit exceptions to named build stages and expire them when onboarding completes.

6. **Approved purple-team defense-impairment control** — A T1562.001 exercise may remove Success or Failure auditing and should trigger. Match engagement ID, operator, target list, exact subcategory, UTC bounds, and restoration evidence. Preserve the alert as control evidence and suppress only duplicate notification after the first result.

**Safe suppression:** preserve the base event and result. Apply an alert-wrapper `lookup windows_audit_policy_change_exceptions endpoint SubcategoryGuid change_summary OUTPUT valid_from_epoch valid_until_epoch owner ticket expected_gpo_version`, then use a `where` clause to suppress notification only for exact values inside an approved finite interval. Reject wildcard endpoints, subject-only exceptions, all-GPO exceptions, and open-ended rows. Re-run controls after GPO, OS, add-on, or baseline changes.

detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites and exact event contract

Assign a Windows policy owner, Active Directory/Intune baseline owner, Splunk collection owner, SOC detection owner, incident responder, and exception approver. Inventory all endpoints and their authoritative audit-policy source: local policy, domain GPO, MDM, configuration management, or image baseline. Install Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows (`Splunk_TA_windows`, Splunkbase 742) version 10.0.1 on collection and required parsing/search tiers. Splunkbase lists platform 9.3 through current 10.x and Cloud support at review time. Test the exact Windows, forwarder, add-on, CIM, and Splunk versions and follow upgrade guidance when crossing the 5.0.0 breaking-change boundary.

The collector account must read the Security channel. The search role needs read access to the deployment-local `wineventlog` index and permission to save/schedule the alert; it does not need GPO edit, local-security-policy, `auditpol /set`, endpoint administration, or lookup-write privileges. Restrict subject identities, policy topology, and raw Security records.

Microsoft states that Event ID 4719 is generated when a computer's **system audit policy** changes and is always logged regardless of the `Audit Audit Policy Change` subcategory setting. The native fields identify the token used by the caller, changed category/subcategory, stable subcategory GUID, and whether Success and/or Failure was added or removed. `%%8448` means Success removed, `%%8449` Success added, `%%8450` Failure removed, and `%%8451` Failure added; combinations are comma-separated.

Do not over-attribute the subject. Microsoft explains that direct `auditpol.exe` calls can show the invoking account, while Group Policy applies settings through a process running as LocalSystem, so a computer account/SYSTEM subject may not identify the human who changed the GPO. Correlate management-plane logs and tickets. Event 4719 is not itself the process that changed policy and is not a universal audit-integrity event; the IDs excluded in `exclusions` require companion controls.

This analytic reports **all** 4719 changes. Additions can be legitimate hardening or surprising policy expansion; removals can impair evidence. The ATT&CK T1562.001 mapping is conditional on adversarial defense impairment and must not be stamped onto every row as a conclusion. No count threshold applies: one valid event is one reviewable change.

## Step 1 — Collect and validate Security XML

Configure a governed local input outside the add-on's `default` directory:

```ini
[WinEventLog://Security]
disabled = 0
renderXml = true
index = wineventlog
checkpointInterval = 5
```

`wineventlog` is a deployment-local index choice. Record `current_only`, `start_from`, checkpoint, and any allow/deny filter used in the actual stanza. Do not filter out 4719 at collection time. Use protected forwarding and size Security-log retention and queues for outages. Validate the effective stanza with `splunk btool inputs list --debug` on a representative forwarder and inspect forwarding health.

The supported XML contract is `sourcetype=XmlWinEventLog` and `source=XmlWinEventLog:Security`; the channel-bearing legacy `WinEventLog:Security` is not the XML source type. Verify native fields:

```spl
index=wineventlog sourcetype=XmlWinEventLog source="XmlWinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4719 earliest=-30d
| table _time Computer EventRecordID SubjectUserSid SubjectUserName SubjectDomainName SubjectLogonId CategoryId SubcategoryId SubcategoryGuid AuditPolicyChanges
| head 50
```

Compare selected EventRecordIDs and XML against Event Viewer **Windows Logs > Security**. Confirm endpoint identity, UTC time, SID/account/domain/logon ID, exact GUID, and raw change codes. Export the local language-independent GUID inventory with `auditpol /list /subcategory:* /v` on each supported OS family and maintain it in version control. Do not use free-text localized subcategory names as the only key.

Build a separate Security-source health search for every expected endpoint. Event 4719 is change-driven and can be absent for long periods, so health must use channel/forwarder freshness, not a requirement for recent 4719. For WEF/WEC, preserve original Computer and EventRecordID, prevent duplicate direct collection, and measure `_indextime-_time`; validate the adapted source contract before use.

## Step 2 — Save and understand the SPL

Save as `windows_system_audit_policy_change_4719`. Schedule hourly, for example `5 * * * *`, with the search's embedded `earliest=-70m@m latest=-10m@m`. The range is a nonoverlapping closed 60-minute event-time window delayed by 10 minutes. Measure p99 arrival latency and shift both bounds equally if needed.

The base search constrains the local index, XML source type, Security source, and 4719. `event_code` accepts add-on `EventCode` or native `EventID`, then the `where` clause reasserts numeric 4719 and nonempty endpoint identity. Endpoint prefers normalized `dest`, then native `Computer`, then host; validate lowercase normalization against the asset namespace.

`subject_account` combines the native domain and account only for presentation. Retain SubjectUserSid and SubjectLogonId as stronger correlation keys. `raw_policy_change` uses `AuditPolicyChanges` and only falls back to rendered `Changes`. The `case` block decodes the four Microsoft values and the two common same-direction pairs; unfamiliar combinations remain raw rather than being guessed. Extend decoding only from observed Microsoft-defined values and boundary tests.

The table keeps one event per row and EventRecordID for provenance. Do not aggregate away endpoint, logon ID, GUID, or exact change when paging. Notification can assign higher urgency when `change_summary` contains `removed`, the endpoint is high value, or the GUID is in an owner-approved critical list. That enrichment belongs after the base result so additions and noncritical changes remain visible.

Splunk documents Change-oriented mapping for 4719, but no `cimSpl` is supplied. A generic Change acceleration query does not necessarily preserve raw codes, native identities, exact GUID, or EventRecordID. If a CIM panel is useful, filter `signature_id=4719`, inspect the installed model/field names, and compare every native row over fixed bounds before relying on it.

## Step 3 — Validate values, boundaries, and attribution

Run the positive XML fixture in an isolated index with fixed bounds. Assert exactly one row and exact endpoint, subject account/SID/logon ID, IDs/GUID, raw pair, decoded `Success removed; Failure removed`, EventRecordID, source, and source type. Independently test each of `%%8448`, `%%8449`, `%%8450`, and `%%8451`, both same-direction pairs, and an unfamiliar value that must pass through unchanged.

Run each negative variant separately. Test non-4719 IDs, wrong source/source type, malformed event code, empty identity, earliest inclusion, latest exclusion, and outside-window events. Test duplicate collection using Computer/EventRecordID and repair topology rather than adding an unproven dedup. Confirm a valid addition returns one row; this guards against silently narrowing the search to removals.

In an authorized Windows lab, export the before state with `auditpol /backup` or `auditpol /get`, change one harmless test subcategory with `auditpol /set`, observe 4719, and restore the exact prior state. Use a disposable endpoint and obtain approval: changing production auditing can erase evidence. For GPO behavior, make an approved lab GPO change, run policy update, and verify that subject context may be SYSTEM/computer rather than the editing administrator. Capture GroupPolicy Operational records and management audit trails for attribution.

Record OS/add-on/forwarder/Splunk versions, effective input, policy source, before/after export, exact UTC bounds, fixture/lab steps, expected and actual rows, search job ID, alert delivery, and restoration. Keep `status=draft` until collection completeness, all four values, boundaries, GPO attribution, notification, dashboard RBAC, response, and suppression are accepted by human owners.

## Step 4 — Operationalize triage and restoration

Build the dashboard described in `visualization`, placing missing/stale Security sources first. Enrich SubcategoryGuid from the governed export and endpoint ownership from CMDB. Preserve raw IDs and codes beside friendly names so localization or lookup drift cannot alter evidence.

When a row appears: (1) verify raw XML, endpoint, EventRecordID, subject token, GUID, and change value; (2) resolve the GUID against the correct OS baseline; (3) determine the authoritative policy source and compare effective `auditpol /get` with approved desired state; (4) correlate SubjectLogonId, process creation, GroupPolicy Operational, AD GPO, Intune, Configuration Manager, and change records; (5) assess which future events are lost or added; (6) restore through the authoritative policy mechanism if unauthorized; and (7) investigate adjacent defense impairment and preserve evidence.

Do not automatically run `auditpol /clear`, `/restore`, or `/set`, edit a GPO, reboot, disable a management agent, or isolate a domain controller from one event. Local correction can be overwritten by GPO and broad restoration can disrupt evidence or compliance. Use the platform owner's tested rollback. If malicious impairment is confirmed, follow incident response, protect the affected endpoint, inspect Security-log clearing and agent tampering, and assess telemetry gaps during the weakened interval.

Review all exceptions and critical-GUID lists after OS baseline changes. Retain evidence according to policy, not a fabricated universal seven-year period. This operational control can contribute evidence about audit-policy integrity but does not by itself satisfy FDA, SWIFT, HITRUST, or any other regulatory clause; the prior unsupported compliance mappings were removed.

## Step 5 — Troubleshoot common failures

- **No 4719 after an approved lab change:** verify the change succeeded, correct endpoint Security channel is collected, XML input does not filter 4719, forwarder/index routing, and Event Viewer. Microsoft says 4719 itself is always logged regardless of the audit subcategory setting.
- **Wrong source/source type:** modern XML uses `sourcetype=XmlWinEventLog` and `source=XmlWinEventLog:Security`; correct ingestion/knowledge rather than widening to ambiguous values.
- **AuditPolicyChanges is null:** inspect raw XML Data names, add-on placement/version, search app context, and source-type conflicts. Do not infer removal from CategoryId alone.
- **Only numeric tokens appear:** expected XML can retain `%%` message tokens. Use the explicit Microsoft mapping and stable GUID lookup; do not depend on localized rendering.
- **Subject is SYSTEM or computer account:** this is expected for Group Policy-mediated application. Correlate management-plane and GroupPolicy logs; do not falsely name that account as the human editor.
- **Many events arrive together:** GPO or baseline application can change many subcategories. Compare the exact GUID/value manifest and rollout scope before suppressing.
- **Policy keeps reverting:** identify winning GPO/MDM/configuration-management source with resultant policy. Local `auditpol /set` may be overwritten; fix desired state at the authority.
- **Duplicate events:** check direct plus WEF collection and Computer/EventRecordID pairs. Repair topology and regenerate baseline evidence.
- **Late events miss the hour:** measure endpoint clock, WEF delay, queues, `_indextime-_time`, and scheduler dispatch. Shift both bounds together to preserve a 60-minute range.
- **CIM counts differ:** compare installed 4719 mappings, exact model constraints, acceleration range/freshness, native fields, and event bounds. Keep raw XML as the evidence contract.
grandmaExplanation: We show every time a Windows computer changes the rules that decide which security activity gets recorded. That helps the team catch an accidental or intentional loss of the records they would need to investigate trouble.
hardware: Windows Vista/Windows Server 2008 or later systems generating Microsoft-documented Event 4719. Collect directly from every endpoint because the event describes that computer's local system audit policy. WEF/WEC requires validated original `Computer`, latency, duplicate handling, and field parity.
